SEOUL (25 June 1950)

Comrade General, the order to cross the 38th Parallel has been given. Soviet-supplied tanks and artillery will support the advance, and most South Korean formations are close to the frontier.

Your direction is Seoul. Break the border positions and take the capital before the defenders can draw back into a connected line. Our equipment gives us an advantage, but replacement tanks and guns are scarce. Bring them through the first battle ready for the march beyond it.

Comrade, collect your forces and meet me at the next briefing, it will be held in the next few hours.

SUWON (30 June 1950)

Seoul is behind us, but South Korean troops have gathered on the southern bank of the Han and destroyed the bridges. The river gives them time to recover while we look for a passage.

Cross the Han and advance on Suwon. The United Nations has called for our withdrawal, and American intervention may follow. Open the roads south before outside forces can strengthen the defence.

TAEJON (16 July 1950)

American troops have entered the fighting. We met them at Osan, and reconnaissance now reports a larger force on the approaches to Taejon. Aircraft are attacking our columns and ports behind the front.

Take Taejon. Our Third Division will engage the Kum River positions from the front while your force turns their flank. Cut the roads behind the defenders before they can withdraw towards Pusan.

intro:
PUSAN PERIMETER 1 (5 August 1950)

The enemy is holding the south-eastern corner of Korea around Pusan. Its port is receiving troops and equipment, while our own divisions have marched and fought for more than a month.

Break the perimeter before those reinforcements can restore the enemy's strength. You have command of the forces assigned to the offensive. Keep pressure across the front so the defenders cannot move every reserve against the first breach.

Yes, eat as much rice as you wish, Comrade General.  We will build up our army and strike another day!

intro:
Pusan perimeter: the second attack — 30 August 1950

The United Nations and South Korean armies still hold the Pusan perimeter. Every week the port brings them more men and equipment. Replacements and tanks have reached us too, but the divisions are tired and we cannot count on another long pause.

Break the positions towards Taegu, Pohang-dong and the Naktong approaches. Take the hills and junctions around Yongsan and Masan, keeping the bases behind our attack secure. The ring must be opened before the enemy can take the initiative.

briliant.text:
We have been betrayed!!! Almost a third of your forces were Southerners forcibly conscripted and untrained. Capitalist spies must have passed knowledge of our plans to the Americans. We have suffered enormous losses! Comrade General, you will not be demoted for this failure. What? I see. It is indeed wise that you have ordered your men to entrench themselves in their current position. Follow me to my headquarters for further briefing on our situation.

AFTERMATH

Before the last North Korean attack had faded away on the Pusan Perimeter; the US 8th Army had started its counteroffensive. They even broke through the North Korean line in some sectors. To make matters worse on 15 September 1950 General MacArthur launched an amphibious invasion against Inch'on near Seoul. In subsequent operations Seoul was captured by the US Army X Corps. The few North Korean units present offered tough but brief resistance. Ten days had past since the landing at Inch'on. By 23 September the North Korean army, what was left of it, was in full retreat back towards North Korea by every possible route it could find.

CHONGJU (27 October 1950)

Chinese forces are entering the war, and our battered formations are reorganising near the Yalu. The advancing United Nations troops still threaten the approaches to the river; they must be held while the counteroffensive takes shape.

Defend Chongju and its surrounding positions. If the enemy leaves an opening, push him back far enough to give the Chinese columns room to assemble. Keep the route to the Yalu in our hands.

intro:
WONJU DEEP RAID (7 January 1951)

The advance has reached Wonju, a communications centre the enemy is expected to defend strongly. Our V Corps will keep its northern and western approaches under pressure.

Take your corps south through the hills east of the town and break into the enemy's rear. Open the roads beyond Wonju while the garrison is occupied by V Corps. The opposing armies are gaining strength; the chance to pass around them may not last.

While you occupied many United Nation forces trying to plug the holes in their open lines, the Chinese west of you have been able to advance and liberate Seoul. The front is now stabilized across the peninsula some 50 miles south of Seoul. Time to resupply and make ready for the final push. Now let us eat some good rice, Comrade General!

Communist forces retreated without heavy fighting to a main defensive line which was now reached by the United Nation forces.

intro:
HOENGSONG (11 February 1951)

Chinese forces have broken into the South Korean positions near Hoengsong. Their attack from the north and west gives our corps an opening on the eastern side of the town.

Advance from the east and take Hoengsong before the enemy can reinforce it. Link the attacks around the road junctions so the defenders cannot shift troops from one threatened sector to another.

briliant.text:
Is it not ironic that communist Allies can count on each other while capitalist Allies cannot? A tactical victory has been gained at Hoengsong and to the west at Chip'yong-ni the Chinese were close to eliminating another pocket of encircled imperialist forces. Unfortunately the UN forces are too powerful at the moment and our communist offensive has ground to a halt. You are right, Comrade General, we will pull back some miles to better positions and hold them as we ready ourselves for an even larger offensive this spring!

AFTERMATH

The limited communist offensive ended in several tactical victories without breaking the United Nations frontline. The US 8th Army recaptured the lost terrain with Operation Killer in late February. Bad weather made it easy for the communists to retreat in good order. This UN counteroffensive in the central sector was continued in Operation Ripper which immediately followed with Operation Killer. However the front near Seoul remained static until the end of March when there too, offensive operations were resumed.

Most of our forces have withdrawn from the ground between the Han and Imjin, but a Chinese rearguard and several of your units remain south of the crossings. Enemy airborne troops are reported on the roads behind them.

Open the way through Munsan-ni and bring the remaining formations out towards Kaesong. Cover the withdrawal from both directions: troops advancing from Seoul may reach the rearguard while it is still fighting to clear the road ahead.

Operations Rugged and Dauntless would push the frontline over the 38th Parallel running from the western coast along the Imjin River to Kumhwa and from there east across the peninsula. intro:
Spring offensive: the eastern sector — 17 May 1951

The first spring attack did not recover Seoul. Our forces and the Chinese have shifted their effort towards the central and eastern mountains, where there are more ways around a defended road.

Drive south from Chunch'on and Kansong and take Sokcho and the hill positions controlling the approaches. Keep contact with the Chinese formations alongside you. The mountains offer cover from enemy aircraft, but they can also separate an advancing column from its food and ammunition.

briliant.text:
Again the cowardly capitalists have retreated before we could destroy them. We do not have the supply capability to keep up with the offensive. You have orders to retreat a bit and reorganize for yet another assault. Whatever may happen, we will never abandon our ambition to liberate and unite Korea!

AFTERMATH

The communist spring offensives were a huge strategic failure. It did result in tactical victories but the United Nations retreated without heavy losses and by doing so were able to immediately produce a counteroffensive. This UN spring offensive would be the last major action of the Korean War. It pushed back the communist armies to the current armistice lines. Both the United States and the People's Republic of China saw that neither could gain a complete victory and were willing to sign a cease fire. Negotiations were long and tedious. They were often interrupted by many small skirmishes. Meanwhile the frontlines were being heavily fortified and with each passing day any new offensive was made that much more difficult. Then finally the truce talks that started in July 1951 culminated in a cease fire signed on 27 July 1953. North and South Korea were more than willing to fight each other to the bitter end but on both sides the major powers decided for them. Officially the Korean War still continues...

intro:
MAJON-NI (11 November 1950)

Many troops left behind in the retreat have formed partisan groups. You are being sent to join one near Majon-ni, between Wonsan and Pyongyang. A South Korean battalion is reported cut off nearby, with American troops on their way to relieve it.

Use the local force to attack the enemy communications and prevent that relief. Your regular formations remain away for refitting and cannot join this operation; you will resume their command afterwards. For now, the men already in this district are the force you have.

briliant.text:
Ah there you are, Comrade General. You need to eat something. I have heard about your actions at Majon-ni. The capitalists have suffered many losses and as you have experienced, the Chinese comrades are pushing south with great success! Travel with me to P'yongyang where your force is waiting for you!

AFTERMATH

Ever since the North Korean retreat from the Pusan Perimeter, pockets of North Korean forces had continued to resist even when they found themselves deep inside enemy held territory. The US IX Corps was deployed behind the frontline to maintain security in the interior. Guerilla activity continued for months.

The United Nations offensive ground to a halt due to severe supply problems and over-extending its forces on too broad a front. Between 14 October and 1 November nearly 180,000 Chinese troops crossed the Chinese-Korean border and more were to follow. They first engaged UN troops in skirmishes but in late November the full might of the expeditionary Chinese Liberation Army fell on the UN troops. This was followed by the longest retreat in United States military history.

Ah there you are, Comrade General. You need to eat something. I have heard about your actions at Majon-ni. The capitalists have suffered many losses and as you have experienced, the Chinese comrades are pushing south with great success! Travel with me to P'yongyang where your force is waiting for you!

The US IX Corps was deployed behind the frontline to maintain security in the interior. Guerilla activity continued for months.
